newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ICN to open new plant in Montenegro.
newsitem.headline: ICN to open new plant in Montenegro.

text.p: ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc., whose chairman is a former prime minister of Yugoslavia, plans to expand Yugoslav operations with a new plant in the republic of Montenegro, an ICN Yugoslavia official said Tuesday.

Officials expect the new plant, to be located in the Montenegrin capital of Podgorica, to reach $20 million in sales by the end of 1997 and have $32 million in annual sales in 1999, Mihajlo Saranovic, ICN executive vice-president and manager for East European operations, told Reuters.

The Costa Mesa, Calif.-based parent company will have a 75 percent stake in the new venture, with the rest owned by the Montenegrin state. Milan Panic, the chairman of ICN, served briefly as Yugoslav prime minister in the early 1990s.

The contract for the plant, to produce 19 medicines earmarked for Yugoslav and foreign markets, was signed on Monday by Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and ICN Yugoslavia Executive Vice President Ljubisa Rakic.
"This will become a medium-sized drug plant, producing according to FDA and the European Union standards," Saranovic said. It will operate under the name ICN Montenegro.
ICN Yugoslavia was set up as a joint venture with the Yugoslav company Galenika in 1991.

ICN Yugoslavia said its total sales were expected to reach nearly $350 million this year. ICN Pharmaceuticals owns 75 percent of the Yugoslav subsidiary, which it describes as its "window to eastern Europe."

ICN Pharmaceuticals also has signed a letter of intent to form a joint company, ICN Bosnia, with the company Krajinalek from Banja Luka in the Bosnian Serb entity. California-based ICN will have a majority stake in the venture.
